conceptual assets.information: The state indicating that a DMI request is outstanding determines whether a new DMI access can be accepted. It has no entry or exit port because it is an internal transport lock.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The busy lock is sensitive transport state whose incorrect modification can accept or reject DMI transactions, as shown by its assignments at lines 270 and 276. A stuck busy state can block subsequent DMI requests through the checks at lines 264 and 273-277.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could prevent the completion acknowledgement from clearing the state or otherwise cause the outstanding-request state to remain asserted, blocking later DMI accesses.

conceptual assets.information: JTAG TMS commands select and advance the TAP scan state used to capture, shift, update and dispatch debug accesses. The commands enter through jtag_tms_i and are not themselves returned through an output port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing the TMS command changes the TAP transition and therefore the selected debug operation through the transitions at lines 123-138. TMS can hold the TAP in reset, pause or another non-transfer state, withholding debug transfers through the same transitions at lines 123-138.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could drive an unintended TMS sequence to alter scan sequencing or hold the TAP in a state that prevents normal DMI transfers.

considered, not kept.reason: The TAP state machine only sequences debug-port accesses, so the sequencing-state and debug-transport rules bar it as a concept of its own; it is implemented at lines 119-140.

considered, not kept.concept: JTAG-shifted DMI request and response words
considered, not kept.reason: The instruction, address, operation, request data and returned data are forwarded-access staging values and are not this unit's information under the forwarded-access-stage rule; the staging and forwarding are shown at lines 181, 189, 192-210 and 266-274.

These debug-transport registers only hold or decide what the debug ports deliver, so the debug-module register rule bars them as separate concepts; they are assigned or used at lines 169-210 and 247-252.
The error flag is a command-error code reported through the debug transport and is therefore excluded by the debug-module register rule despite being assigned at lines 257-259.
The acknowledgement only times completion of the forwarded DMI transfer and clears the busy state at line 275, so the transfer-record and handshake rules provide no independent security objective.
The code is fixed by build-time generics and constants and is only shifted out for identification at lines 187 and 207, so it is not a protected run-time asset.
